target_customer: Consumer brands and agencies that field sponsorship requests, and startups, creators and event organizers seeking brand partners
problem: Brands handled sponsorship requests through email, spreadsheets, Basecamp and PayPal, and event organizers had no central place to find sponsors.
business_model: Marketplace fee of 10 to 20 percent of sponsorship spend at the Sponsorfied launch; by 2014 free platform access with revenue from education services and custom video reports

founders.name: Cullen Wilson
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CEO in the July 2012 TechCrunch launch article. The YC page also lists him.

founders.name: Baldwin Cunningham
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2013 and 2014 name him as CEO and co-founder.

founders.name: David Matthews
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder in TechCrunch 2012 and on the YC page.

exit.reason: No shutdown or acquisition announcement found. The YC directory marks the company Inactive.

technical_complexity.rationale: A two sided web marketplace plus later sponsorship management dashboard; standard web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Value depended on getting both brands and sponsorship seekers onto the network, but the software itself was easy to copy and revenue relied on service work.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response was found in sources. The company went inactive without a documented acquisition.

market_need_then: The July 2012 TechCrunch launch article says brands managed sponsorship by email, spreadsheets, Basecamp and PayPal, and early private beta clients included Red Bull, TaskRabbit and popchips.

branding.name_origin: Renamed from Sponsorfied in June 2013. CEO Baldwin Cunningham said sponsorship set one way expectations of free goods while partnership means brands and actors mutually benefit.
branding.domain_note: partnered.com now redirects to crossbeam.com, which appears to be a different company; how the original company held the domain is not documented.

identity.voice_and_tone: Partnership oriented, compared by the CEO to flash sale style curation

rebrands.why: The old name centered on sponsorships, which the CEO considered too limiting.

brand_strength.rationale: Press covered the rename and a seed round, but no sources show brand driven awareness. The new name is a common word.

pivots.to: Partnered, a broader brand partnership platform with Partnered DIRECT and MANAGE
pivots.why: The CEO said the sponsorship framing was too limiting.

outcome_analysis: Sponsorfied launched out of YC in 2012 with big brand beta clients and rebranded to Partnered in 2013. It raised an $850K seed in July 2014 for a stated total of $1.6M, then went inactive with no public post-mortem, so the cause is not public. The pattern fits a thin marketplace with service heavy revenue, but no source states the reason.
notes: Total raised was stated as $1.6M by TechCrunch in July 2014, which implies about $750K earlier, but no source names that earlier round, so it is not recorded. The 2013 TechCrunch article lists Mike Rothenberg, Dave McClure, Shervin Pishevar and Gary Vaynerchuk as investors without amounts. Round rests on one outlet (TechCrunch); a search for a second outlet found none. No competitor appears in dated sources; none of the 2012 and 2013 articles name one. A different YC company named Partnered (W21) exists and was not used here. The 2012 launch article says Sponsorfied was in the YC Summer 2012 batch.
